We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: a sulfonyl linking two phenyl rings: one is p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to another phenyl bearing a cinnamoyl anilide.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis: likely disconnections:

1. Amide formation: between cinnamic acid (or α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So break C(=O)N bond to give acid and aniline.

2. Formation of the α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner modification: from aromatic aldehyde (maybe 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl) and malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to sulfonyl phenyl. So break C=C double bond and C-C bond to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

3. Sulfonamide formation: between sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the phenyl ring with sulfonamide). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the p-tolyl ring (the left phenyl). So break S-N bond to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the other phenyl amine (the second phenyl with the unsaturated amide). Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the left phenyl (p-tolyl) and to the right phenyl (c2ccc...). Actually the SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the left phenyl (p-tolyl) and the sulfonyl group attached to the right phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of the left phenyl substituent (anilide). So the sulfonamide formation could be between p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the right phenyl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc...S(=O)(=O)Cl). But the sulfonyl group is attached to the right phenyl, which also bears the unsaturated amide. So we could disconnect at S-N bond to give p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and the sulfonyl chloride of the right phenyl (c2ccc(... )S(=O)(=O)Cl). That seems plausible.

Thus three steps:

Step 1 (retro): amide bond cleavage -> give α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid derivative) attached to right phenyl (c2ccc(/C=C/ C(=O) )? Actually the acid would be c2ccc(/C=C/ C(=O)OH)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide carbonyl is attached to the unsaturated chain attached to the right phenyl. So the acid precursor would be c2ccc(/C=C/ C(=O)OH)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group (i.e., sulfonyl phenyl with carboxylic acid). So the acid is a sulfonyl phenyl α,β-unsaturated acid.

Step 2 (retro): formation of that α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner modification from aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl) and malonic acid.

Step 3 (retro): sulfonamide formation from p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2) (the sulfonyl chloride derived from the right phenyl after step 2? Actually after step 2 we have sulfonyl phenyl with aldehyde? Wait the aldehyde is on the phenyl that will become the sulfonyl phenyl after sulfonyl chloride formation. So step 2 yields sulfonyl phenyl α,β-unsaturated acid? But the sulfonyl group is already present. Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the right phenyl in the final product. In retrosynthesis, we could consider that sulfonyl group is introduced after the Doebner step? But sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl before the Doebner? The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl ring, not to the side chain. So the sulfonyl phenyl is a separate aromatic ring with sulfonyl substituent. The Doebner modification would be on that phenyl ring bearing the sulfonyl group? The aldehyde would be on that phenyl ring (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with sulfonyl group attached (S(=O)(=O)Cl) maybe? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via S(=O)(=O) attached to the phenyl carbon (aryl sulfone). In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl carbon (aryl sulfonyl). So the phenyl bearing the sulfonyl group also bears the unsaturated chain. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl bearing sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl group) and aldehyde. So step 2: aldehyde (aryl-CHO) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid attached to same aryl (still bearing sulfonyl group). So the sulfonyl group must already be present on the aryl before Doebner. So we need sulfonyl chloride on that aryl before step 2? Actually the sulfonyl group is part of the final product attached to the nitrogen, not to the aryl carbon. Wait re-evaluate: NS(=O)(=O)c2... means the sulfonyl group is attached to nitrogen (N-SO2-aryl). So the sulfonyl group is attached to the nitrogen, not to the aryl carbon. The aryl is attached to the sulfonyl S. So the aryl is the sulfonyl aryl (aryl-SO2-). So the aryl bearing the unsaturated chain is attached to the sulfonyl S. So the sulfonyl group is between the two phenyl rings: left phenyl attached to N, right phenyl attached to S. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the right phenyl via S-aryl bond. So the right phenyl is a sulfonyl aryl (aryl-SO2-). So the sulfonyl group is attached to the right phenyl carbon (aryl-SO2-). So the right phenyl is a sulfonyl aryl, not a sulfonyl chloride. So the sulfonyl group is already present on that phenyl before the amide formation. The sulfonyl group is introduced via sulfonyl chloride reacting with left aniline (p-toluidine). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine (or p-tolyl amine) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2). That aryl sulfonyl chloride must have the unsaturated side chain already attached? The side chain is attached to the aryl via the double bond chain, not via the sulfonyl. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride would be c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with the side chain attached at para position? Actually the side chain is attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O). So the aryl has both sulfonyl group (attached to S) and the side chain at para position. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same aryl with sulfonyl chloride instead of sulfonamide: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with the side chain still present? The side chain is attached to the aryl carbon, not to the sulfonyl. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the aryl with side chain and sulfonyl chloride. So step 2 (Doebner) would produce the side chain (α,β-unsaturated amide) attached to the aryl, but the sulfonyl group is already present as sulfonyl chloride? Actually the side chain includes the amide, which is formed later. So after Doebner, we have aryl with α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (instead of amide). The sulfonyl group is still a sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl group is attached to the aryl via S=O2, but the sulfonyl chloride is S(=O)(=O)Cl. So the aryl sulfonyl chloride with α,β-unsaturated acid substituent. Then step 1 amide formation converts the acid to amide with aniline. Then step 3 sulfonamide formation attaches left phenyl amine to sulfonyl chloride, displacing Cl.

Thus three steps: (retro) 1) amide bond cleavage; 2) Doebner modification (break C=C and C-C to aldehyde + malonic acid); 3) sulfonamide formation (break S-N to give aryl sulfonyl chloride and p-toluidine).

Now we need to find template IDs for each transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with appropriate functional groups broken/formed.

Step 1: amide formation forward is coupling of acid + amine -> amide. Retro we break amide to acid + amine. So functional groups broken: amide (since forward forms amide, retro breaks amide). functional groups formed: carboxylic acid and primary amine? But the tool expects functional groups broken/formed in forward direction. For our retro step, we need a template that in forward direction forms amide from acid and amine. So we should search for functional_groups_broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid", "primary amines"] and functional_groups_formed: ["amide"]. Let's try.
